name: Thaddaeus
title: Judas, not Iscariot
summary: Thaddaeus, also called Judas son of James or Lebbaeus, was one of Jesus' twelve apostles. He is referred to as 'Judas, not Iscariot' to distinguish him from the traitor. At the Last Supper, he asked Jesus why He would reveal Himself to the disciples but not to the world.

keyEvents.title: Chosen as an apostle
keyEvents.description: Thaddaeus was chosen as one of Jesus' twelve apostles. Matthew and Mark call him Thaddaeus, while Luke calls him Judas son of James.

keyEvents.title: Among the apostles
keyEvents.description: Thaddaeus is mentioned among the twelve apostles whom Jesus called to Himself and gave authority.

keyEvents.title: The question at the Last Supper
keyEvents.description: Judas (not Iscariot) asked Jesus: 'Lord, how can it be that You will reveal Yourself to us and not to the world?'

keyEvents.title: In the upper room
keyEvents.description: After the ascension, Judas son of James was among the apostles gathered in prayer in the upper room.

keyEvents.title: Sent out
keyEvents.description: Thaddaeus was among the twelve who were sent out by Jesus to preach the kingdom of God and heal the sick.
